approved_table: Owner-approved bar for a professional repo; one area per row. A criterion may only be added, changed or removed with a version bump and owner approval.

areas.row: Re-runs are safe, failures are loud, nothing is fetched or dropped silently, and every rule has a test that fails without it.
areas.paths: ingestion/, scripts/run_ingestion.py, scripts/refresh_constituents.py, scripts/import_constituents.py, scripts/refresh_yfinance_names.py, scripts/archive_raw_to_supabase.py, scripts/record_ingestion_fixtures.py, scripts/replay_ingestion_fixtures.py

criteria.rule: A re-run (same inputs) yields the same state; an interrupted or failed run leaves no partially written or inconsistent output.
A failure is loud: no exception is swallowed (caught without re-raise, non-zero exit or a reported count) in a way that hides lost or wrong data.
Nothing is fetched or dropped silently: every row or ticker dropped, skipped or defaulted is counted or reported.
Ingestion writes raw fields only, no derived metrics.
criteria.source: CLAUDE.md Layout ('raw fields only, no derived metrics'); docs/project_context.md

criteria.rule: Every validation, guard or rule in ingestion code has a test that would fail if the rule were removed.
criteria.source: approved table row (ingestion); .claude/working-agreement.md section 4 (tests are non-negotiable)

areas.row: Every model sits in the right layer, has tests and docs, and has no dead models.

criteria.rule: Each model sits in the layer docs/layering.md assigns to what it does, including rules check_layer_contract.py cannot see mechanically.
Each model has the tests and documentation docs/engineering_standards.md sections 2 and 3 require for its layer.
No dead model: every model is referenced downstream, exported, or is a documented terminal mart.
Naming and SQL structure follow docs/engineering_standards.md section 1 and 1.1.
Comments follow docs/engineering_standards.md section 1.2 (WHY only, no history, no dates or MR references).

areas.row: Migrations match the database, and the export is checked in CI.
areas.paths: scripts/export_to_supabase.py, scripts/check_export_health.py, scripts/apply_supabase_migrations.py, supabase/migrations/, dbt_analytics/models/5_marts (contracts), docs/data_contract.md, docs/supabase_setup.md, .gitlab-ci.yml

criteria.rule: The column sets and types agree across the dbt mart contract, the export column allowlist and the Postgres migrations.
Each export guarantee docs claim is checked by a CI job that actually runs it.
Grains and keys documented in docs/data_contract.md match the mart contract and the export's conflict keys.
The migrations ledger in docs/supabase_setup.md matches the files in supabase/migrations/.

areas.row: No business logic in the UI layer; behaviour matches the UI specs.

criteria.rule: The frontend does not compute business logic that belongs upstream (metric values, eligibility, deduplication, ranking rules).
criteria.source: .claude/working-agreement.md anti-patterns ('Doing real logic in the consumption/frontend layer'); approved table row (frontend)

criteria.rule: Rendered copy, ordering and interaction match the spec in docs/ui/*.md for that component; cite the spec line and the code line.
No dead frontend code: every function, constant and module is used.

areas.row: One source per fact, no history narrative, no stale claims, every doc linked from CLAUDE.md.
areas.paths: docs/ (excluding docs/handover_*.md content, which are labelled point-in-time archives), README.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/working-agreement.md, .claude/skills/, .claude/active_work.md

criteria.rule: One source per fact: a fact is not restated in two places where the copies disagree, and CLAUDE.md links rather than restates substance.
criteria.source: CLAUDE.md header ('the linked doc wins on conflict'); .claude/working-agreement.md section 2 (grep the claim)

criteria.rule: Durable docs state the current state only: no history narrative, rejected options, 'changed from X to Y', dates or MR references.
criteria.source: global CLAUDE.md (repo files state only the current state); .claude/working-agreement.md section 2 (prose earns its place); docs/engineering_standards.md section 1.2

criteria.rule: No stale claim: every claim a doc makes about code, files, commands or behaviour holds in the current code; cite the doc line and the contradicting code line.
No broken reference: every file, function, script, test or section a doc names exists.
The two point-in-time handover archives in docs/ and the handover file .claude/active_work.md: report only as a documented decision worth revisiting (their existence and size), never as a defect.
criteria.source: CLAUDE.md (labels them point-in-time archives); approved table row (repo hygiene)

areas.row: No dead code, scripts or files; no archives that git history already covers.
areas.paths: whole repository (git ls-files), excluding .venv and ignored files

criteria.rule: No dead script, module or file: each is imported, run by CI or a hook, or named as a command in a runbook doc.
No tracked generated artifact, build output or duplicate copy of a file.
No duplicated logic across modules unless the duplication is documented as deliberate (e.g. a mirrored constant with a test that keeps the copies equal).
criteria.source: approved table row (repo hygiene); .claude/working-agreement.md section 4 (no unnecessary complexity)

criteria.rule: No leftover debug output, commented-out code or TODO/FIXME in tracked code.
criteria.source: global CLAUDE.md (comment only the WHY); docs/engineering_standards.md section 1.2

areas.row: Every reviewer and hook actually loads and runs, with a test proving it.

criteria.rule: Every reviewer definition in .claude/agents/ has frontmatter that parses as YAML with name, description, tools and model, so the harness registers it.
Every hook wired in .claude/settings.json or .pre-commit-config.yaml exists, and has a test that would fail if it stopped working.
Every path pattern in .claude/review_routing.json matches at least one tracked file, or is documented as intentionally dormant.
Every script a CI job runs exists, and every check a doc says CI runs is actually in .gitlab-ci.yml.
